bridge_listening: DevBridge: listening on {host}:{port}. Attach VS Code now (Run and Debug -> PyQGIS: Attach to running QGIS).
bridge_already_running: DevBridge: bridge is already running on port {port}.
debugpy_missing: DevBridge: the 'debugpy' package is not installed in QGIS's Python. Open DevBridge > Control Panel > 'Prepare a plugin' and press 'Prepare for debugging' (it installs debugpy), or run: python -m pip install debugpy
pycharm_not_found: No PyCharm installation found automatically. Start a 'Python Debug Server' run configuration in PyCharm, or see Manual PyCharm Instructions.
pycharm_pydevd_missing: pydevd-pycharm failed to install or import. See Manual PyCharm Instructions.
pycharm_connection_refused: Could not connect to PyCharm on {host}:{port}. In PyCharm, start the 'Python Debug Server' run configuration first, then try again.
pycharm_pypi_unreachable: Could not reach PyPI to resolve the matching pydevd-pycharm version ({error}). Check your network connection, or see Manual PyCharm Instructions to install a version by hand.
pycharm_script_saved: A reusable attach script was saved to {path}.
cp_vscode_info: Starts a debugpy server inside this QGIS session. Then in VS Code choose Run and Debug -> 'PyQGIS: Attach to running QGIS'. Host and port can be changed while the bridge is stopped.
cp_pycharm_info: PyCharm is the listener: first start a 'Python Debug Server' run configuration in PyCharm, then press Auto-configure. DevBridge finds your PyCharm build, installs the matching pydevd-pycharm and connects.
cp_project_info: Choose what you want to work on, then prepare it: creates a .venv that can import qgis, installs debugpy and writes the VS Code configuration. A new plugin also gets starter files.
cp_browse_title: Choose a plugin or project folder
cp_project_missing: Choose an existing plugin or project folder first.
cp_vscode_missing: VS Code's 'code' command was not found on PATH. Open the folder in VS Code manually (or enable 'Add to PATH' in its installer).
cp_tool_info: The same operations are available as a separate desktop program that does not need QGIS to be running (handy for setting up before you start QGIS). It shares its settings with this plugin.
cp_tool_missing: The bundled desktop tool was not found. Reinstall DevBridge from plugins.qgis.ge.
cp_no_tk: No Python with Tk (tkinter) was found to run the desktop tool. Install Python from python.org (keep 'tcl/tk and IDLE' ticked), or run the tool from the folder with your own Python: python -m devbridge gui
cp_guide:
TABS, IN THE ORDER YOU'LL USE THEM
"Prepare a plugin" -> "VS Code" (or "PyCharm") -> "Desktop tool" (optional, no QGIS needed there).

WHAT THIS IS FOR
Stop your own plugin's code on any line (a "breakpoint") while QGIS is running, from VS Code or PyCharm, and look at the variables step by step.

ONCE PER PLUGIN (about a minute)
1. Open the tab "Prepare a plugin" and choose what you want: improve one of YOUR plugins (pick it in the list - it shows the plugins of every QGIS profile), start a NEW plugin (type a name), or use any folder.
2. Press "Prepare for debugging" (for a new plugin: "Create and prepare") and wait until the log ends with "Setup complete".
   New plugin: starter files are written first (a menu entry that says hello). Then a .venv is created, debugpy installed and the VS Code settings written into the plugin's folder.

DEBUG WITH VS CODE
3. Press "Open in VS Code" (same tab). VS Code opens your plugin's folder.
4. Open the tab "VS Code" here and press "Start Debug Bridge (VS Code)". The status must say "running".
5. In VS Code press Ctrl+Shift+D (Run and Debug), choose "PyQGIS: Attach to running QGIS" and press the green triangle.
6. Click just left of a line number in your code: a red dot is a breakpoint.
7. In QGIS use your plugin (its menu or button). QGIS pauses, VS Code shows the line. F10 = next line, F11 = step into, F5 = continue.

DEBUG WITH PYCHARM (instead of steps 3-5)
3. In PyCharm: Run > Edit Configurations > + > "Python Debug Server". Keep host localhost and the port from the "PyCharm" tab (12345) > OK, then press the bug icon (Debug). It says "Waiting for process connection".
4. Open the tab "PyCharm" here and press "Auto-configure & Start PyCharm Bridge". Order matters: PyCharm first, then this button.
5. Set breakpoints in PyCharm and use your plugin in QGIS.

GOOD TO KNOW
- Use ONE debugger per QGIS session: VS Code or PyCharm, not both. To switch, restart QGIS.
- After you edit your code, use the "Reload plugin" box at the top of this panel (pick your
  plugin, press "Reload in QGIS") to run your latest code without restarting QGIS.
- "Stop" only updates the status; the port stays open until QGIS restarts.
- The same steps work without QGIS in the "Desktop tool" tab.
- If something fails, the QGIS message bar and the log on the tab say what to fix.
pycharm_python_not_found: Could not find the Python interpreter that belongs to this QGIS, so pydevd-pycharm cannot be installed automatically. See Manual PyCharm Instructions.
pycharm_pip_failed: Installing pydevd-pycharm failed: {error}. Check your internet connection, or see Manual PyCharm Instructions.
debugger_conflict: DevBridge: only one debugger can be used per QGIS session, and the other one (VS Code's debugpy or PyCharm's pydevd) is already loaded. Restart QGIS to switch between VS Code and PyCharm.
cp_choose_plugin_first: Choose a plugin from the list first.
cp_new_name_invalid: '{name}' is not a valid plugin name: use lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter (2-40 characters).
cp_new_exists: {path} already contains a non-empty folder named '{name}'.
cp_new_not_created_yet: This plugin has not been created yet. Press "Create and prepare" first.
cp_new_next: Next: open it in VS Code. In QGIS enable the plugin in Plugins > Manage and Install Plugins (restart QGIS or use Plugin Reloader if it is not listed yet), then start the debug bridge.
cp_reload_ok: '{name}' reloaded - your latest code is running.
cp_reload_not_active: '{name}' is not enabled yet - tick it in Plugins > Manage and Install Plugins first.
